title: Κύνες λιμώττουσαι
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 176. Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Κύνες λιμώττουσαι, ὡς ἐθεάσαντο ἔν τινι ποταμῷ βύρσας βρεχομένας, μὴ δυνάμεναι αὐτῶν ἐφικέσθαι, συνέθεντο ἀλλήλαις ὅπως πρῶτον τὸ ὕδωρ ἐκπίωσι, εἶθ’ οὕτως ἐπὶ τὰς βύρσας παραγένωνται.
sentences.tr: Kynes limōttousai, hōs etheasanto en tini potamōi byrsas brechomenas, mē dynamenai autōn ephikesthai, synethento allēlais hopōs prōton to hydōr ekpiōsi, eith’ houtōs epi tas byrsas paragenōntai.
sentences.l: Starving dogs, when they saw hides soaking in a river, not being able to reach them, agreed with one another that they should first drink up the water, and so then come at the hides.
sentences.i: Some starving dogs saw hides soaking in a river, and being unable to reach them, agreed among themselves to drink the water up first and so get at the hides.
sentences.n: The dogs are feminine throughout (λιμώττουσαι, δυνάμεναι, ἀλλήλαις): κύων is of both genders, and the fable makes this pack female — English has no easy way to keep that visible. συντίθεμαι with ὅπως and the aorist subjunctive is the regular construction for an agreement about what is to be done. ἐφικνέομαι takes the genitive of what is reached. εἶθ’ οὕτως, "and then in that way", marks the second step of the plan.

sentences.t: Συνέβη δὲ αὐταῖς πινούσαις διαρραγῆναι πρὶν ἢ τῶν βυρσῶν ἐφικέσθαι.
sentences.tr: Synebē de autais pinousais diarragēnai prin ē tōn byrsōn ephikesthai.
sentences.l: But it befell them, as they drank, to burst apart before reaching the hides.
sentences.i: But as they drank they burst before they could reach the hides.
sentences.n: συνέβη is impersonal, with the dative of the person and an infinitive of what happens to them. πρὶν ἤ with the infinitive is "before". διαρρήγνυμι is to tear a thing right through: they split open.

sentences.t: Οὕτως ἔνιοι τῶν ἀνθρώπων δι’ ἐλπίδα κέρδους ἐπισφαλεῖς μόχθους ὑφιστάμενοι φθάνουσι πρότερον καταναλισκόμενοι ἢ ὧν βούλονται περιγενόμενοι.
sentences.tr: Houtōs enioi tōn anthrōpōn di’ elpida kerdous episphaleis mochthous hyphistamenoi phthanousi proteron katanaliskomenoi ē hōn boulontai perigenomenoi.
sentences.l: Thus some among men, taking on perilous toils through hope of gain, are used up sooner than they get the better of what they want.
sentences.i: Thus some men take on perilous toils in hope of gain, and are spent before they ever master what they are after.
sentences.n: φθάνω with a supplementary participle says which of two things happens first, and the two participles here are set against each other by πρότερον … ἤ: the being used up comes before the prevailing. περιγίγνομαι takes the genitive of what one gets the better of, and that is why the relative is ὧν, though as the object of βούλονται it would have been accusative — one word doing both offices. ἐπισφαλής is "apt to trip", and so precarious.
